question: Does the new nearest-example vote contain information beyond the independently elected 16-fit two-encoder portfolio, or mostly the same useful signal? Use no new fit. Register this study before scoring the independently running raw near-tie solver.
sources: Read the self-elected 16-fit control recipe from the original seal, its actual training primary and both matched confirmation classifiers. Obtain the analogy observations from the strict raw primary and the two independently measured, already completed near-tie pilot confirmations using the same payloads. Check payload/label/row identities and reconstruct the previously reported two-encoder scores before pairing.
decisions: Keep the entire two-component incumbent as the anchor. On the primary panel, apply the already specified generic near-tie or positive nomination rule to shares [0,.25,.5,1] of the adviser. Freeze its share and only then read the new combination on each confirmation. Report per-fold gained/lost/changed versus the two-component anchor, including the nominated share when it misses the threshold. A new full pipeline for ensemble incumbents may be proposed only if the same strict deployment gate passes. This is a retrospective conditional development test; the separate constituent scores on these development folds have been seen.
resources: 0 new base classifier or index fits, 0 API calls. Training data only. Never inspect validation scores of any of the new combinations, and never select a recipe using course labels.
